Bahrain Imposes Temporary Export Restrictions on Oil & Gas Producers, Industry Faces Disruptions

Bahrain’s Ministry of Industry and Commerce has imposed temporary export restrictions on certain oil and gas products, a move that has sent ripples through the nation’s Oil & Gas Producers industry. The measure, announced late Monday, aims to prioritize domestic energy supply amid rising regional demand and ongoing infrastructure maintenance.

The export restrictions, which took effect immediately, apply to liquefied natural gas (LNG), crude oil, and select refined petroleum products. Bahrain LNG WLL, one of the country’s primary exporters of liquefied natural gas, confirmed that several scheduled shipments have been suspended pending further notice.

“This restriction is a critical step to ensure Bahrain’s energy security during a period of increased local consumption and planned maintenance at key facilities,” said Khalid Al Mansoori, spokesperson for the Ministry. “We are working closely with industry stakeholders to minimize disruptions.”

Market participants reported immediate effects on operations. “We’ve had to halt two cargoes that were due for export this week,” said a senior executive at Bahrain LNG WLL. “This is impacting our short-term revenues and our contractual obligations with overseas partners.”

Industry analysts estimate that Bahrain’s oil and gas exports could fall by as much as 18% in June if the restrictions remain in place through the end of the month. The Bahrain Oil Producers Association warned that prolonged restrictions could affect investment plans and supply chain arrangements.

“Export curbs of this type can have significant knock-on effects, especially for companies with international commitments,” said Amira Qattan, an energy analyst at Gulf Markets Advisory. “If the current situation continues, we may see a reassessment of project timelines and cash flow projections.”

The Ministry has stated that the restrictions will be reviewed weekly. In the meantime, companies such as Bahrain LNG WLL and Eastern Gulf Petroleum are adjusting their operations and monitoring official updates closely as the situation develops.
